title: Priority micro-batching with speculative execution to cut rerank tail latency
creator: Ava Patel
description:
Problem: Rerank endpoint shows high p95/p99 latency under mixed workloads where a small portion of long-token requests or slow workers create stragglers that delay whole batches. Current continuous batching groups requests aggressively which improves throughput but amplifies latency tail for interactive callers. Goal: reduce tail latency without losing >10% throughput by introducing request prioritization, micro-batches for latency-sensitive requests, and speculative execution for stalled slots. Scope: server-side rerank pipeline, admission logic, scheduler, and per-request timeout semantics. Excludes model changes and client protocol updates beyond a routing hint.

Proposed approach: implement a priority-aware micro-batching scheduler that maintains two concurrent batch queues: (1) fast path for low-token, high-priority requests aggregated into small micro-batches (size 2-8) with tight timeouts (e.g., 8ms max wait) and (2) throughput path for high-token or background requests that can tolerate higher latency. Add speculative execution: if a micro-batch or single-request is delayed beyond a configurable worker-queue-threshold, spawn a speculative duplicate on a different worker (best-effort) and accept the earliest response, canceling the other. Combine with token-aware admission: classify requests at admission using token estimates to avoid mixing long requests into latency micro-batches. Implement per-request soft-deadlines and hedging windows so that rerank callers with SLAs can request priority via header.

Trade-offs considered: speculative execution increases GPU utilization and could increase cost if used indiscriminately; mitigated by limiting speculative rate and only hedging high-priority or sampled requests. Micro-batches reduce batching efficiency; mitigated by dynamic sizing based on recent latency/throughput telemetry. There is added scheduler complexity and potential for out-of-order scoring; responses include deterministic tie-breaks and tracing to preserve correctness for consumers that rely on stable ordering.
acceptance_criteria: p95 latency for priority rerank requests reduced by >=40% vs baseline under mixed workload (measured on benchmark harness)
overall throughput drop <=10% for standard production mix (95th percentile traffic profile)
resource overhead (GPU seconds) from speculative execution <=6% for default config
feature gate controls exist and operators can tune micro-batch size and speculative-rate via console or API
end-to-end tests and integration tests added to CI validating cancellation correctness and no double-charges for clients
design_decisions: Two-queue scheduler to separate latency-sensitive and throughput requests
Speculative execution only for requests with priority header or sampled traffic to limit cost impact
Token estimate computed from prompt length and tokenization heuristics at admission time
Worker-level cancellation via cancel token to avoid wasted GPU work when a speculative response wins
Telemetry: emit per-request route -> micro-batch id -> speculative flag to trace samples in Console
rollout_plan: Feature development on branch: implement scheduler + admission + experiment flags
Canary deploy to internal dedicated cluster with synthetic mixed workload generator (low/high token split)
Stage rollout: 1% traffic (priority header only) -> 5% -> 20% -> 100% for latency tier after verifying metrics
Monitor p50/p95/p99, GPU utilization, speculative-hit-rate, and error rates. Roll back if error rate + request cost exceed thresholds
Post-launch: open A/B experiment comparing default vs micro-batch-only vs micro-batch+speculative
metrics_targets: Baseline p95 priority rerank: 220ms -> target p95 <= 130ms
Baseline p99 priority rerank: 420ms -> target p99 <= 240ms
Throughput regression: <=10% decrease in tokens/sec on mixed load
Speculative duplicate rate: default <=3% of requests; sampled experiments up to 10%
No increase in error rate or incorrect ordering observed in integration test runs
test_plan: Unit tests: scheduler state transitions, admission token classification, speculative spawn/cancel flow
Integration test: end-to-end rerank harness replaying production traces (sanitized) with mixed token lengths
Chaos test: kill worker mid-execution to validate speculative candidate completes remaining work and cancellations are clean
Load test: stress both micro-batch and throughput queues and measure throughput/latency trade-offs
Canary monitoring: automated guardrails that pause traffic and create an incident if p99 increases >10% or GPU cost spikes
